title: The Women’s Bikepacking Guide by McKenzie Barney
content:
McKenzie Barney recently released The Women’s Bikepacking Guide to help encourage women to travel solo. Today, the author lays out her intent for the guide, along with a chapter-by-chapter introduction…

Four years ago, I flew into Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, with a backpack, a pair of sandals, and a wild idea to cycle the length of the country. I walked into a local bike shop, purchased a $100 secondhand mountain bike, and started pedaling north. I had no idea what “bikepacking” was, how to change a flat tire, or what I was getting myself into. I just knew I wanted to get to Hanoi, and a bicycle seemed like an adventurous way to get there.

One country led to a continent. Then another. And another. Fast-forward four years, five continents, and 28 countries, and I’d cycled 18,000 miles (29,000 kilometers), the distance benchmark associated with circumnavigating the globe by bicycle.

I tell that story in my award-winning documentary film, Cycling The World (available to watch on YouTube). But what the film doesn’t show is just how much I had to learn along the way. The mechanical failures in the middle of nowhere. The questionable gear choices. The sleepless nights wondering whether I’d chosen a safe place to pitch my tent. The international border crossings, the wrong turns, the mistakes that became my greatest teachers.

Somewhere along those thousands of miles, I began collecting lessons I wished someone had told me before I set off.

And when I returned home, I decided to put them all in one place.

The Guide I Wish I’d Had

Over the past year, I’ve been compiling four years of lessons, tips, tricks, and hard-earned wisdom into a resource for other women dreaming of adventures by bicycle.

The result is The Women’s Bikepacking Guide, an 80-page digital handbook. I kept it digital in the spirit of lightweight bikepacking, so it’s easy to download on your phone or tablet and take along for the ride. The guide is divided into six chapters…

Chapter One: Mindset

Before the gear lists and route planning comes the biggest hurdle of all: deciding to go. It’s mind-blowing how many people leave a bikepacking idea at exactly that: just an idea. They’ve dreamt of the route, the country, the gritty adventure, but then never pursue it. This section is designed to help push asses out the door and onto the saddle.

I break down the sometimes intimidating world of bikepacking, how to prepare for your first trip, what to consider when deciding between riding solo and with others, and how to build up to longer adventures without burning yourself out. Because you don’t need to be an expert to begin… I certainly wasn’t.

Chapter Two: Planning

Where should I go? How far should I ride each day? How do I navigate a foreign country without getting hopelessly lost?

This chapter covers route planning, navigation and mapping tools, choosing daily mileage, global cycling resources, and a collection of iconic long-distance routes from around the world to get your wheels turning. This list of possible routes will be sure to spark some ideas.

Chapter Three: Gear

Ah, the eternal question of any human-powered adventure: What do I actually need to bring?

From choosing the right bicycle and bags to wheels, tires, handlebars, pedals, and packing systems, I share the gear lessons I learned through years of trial and error. There’s an extensive packing list covering clothing, sleeping systems, hydration, repair tools, electronics, and personal hygiene, along with the bikes and setups I chose for different parts of my journey. I also dive into female-specific gear, including saddles, chamois, and the little comforts that can make a big difference when you’re spending months in the saddle.

Chapter Four: Shelter

Wild camping was one of my biggest fears when I started traveling alone (this seems to be the case for many women I speak to). By the end of my journey, it had become one of my favorite parts of bicycle travel.

I share my strategies for finding campsites, staying safe, choosing shelter, and knowing when to seek alternative accommodation. You’ll also find cooking setups, food ideas and hacks, camping tricks, and a few of my favorite campsites from around the world.

Chapter Five: Travel

This is where things get especially interesting when you start crossing countries and continents.

How do you fly with a bicycle? What happens when you reach an international land border? How much does a long-distance trip actually cost?

I break down budgeting, border crossings, flying with your bike, money exchange, SIM cards, travel apps, and the practical logistics of arriving somewhere entirely unfamiliar. I also share ways to connect with local communities, which turned out to be one of the most rewarding parts of my entire journey.

Chapter Six: Inspiration

Because sometimes the most useful thing isn’t another gear recommendation. It’s hearing about someone who went before you. I’ve included a collection of inspiring women traveling far by bicycle, books written by female adventurers, films documenting extraordinary journeys, cycling podcasts, and resources to fuel your next adventure.

There’s also female-specific safety advice throughout the guide, drawn from my own experiences traveling mostly solo around the world.
Because I believe we need more than practical information. We need to see other women doing the things we dream of doing.

Why A Guide for Women?

When I first announced I was setting off alone, I heard plenty of reasons why I shouldn’t go.

It’s dangerous. What if something happens? Aren’t you afraid?

And sure, there are real risks worth understanding and preparing for. But I’ve always wondered why we spend so much time telling women all the places they shouldn’t go, and so little time talking about all the places they should.

What about the friendships waiting to be made? The strangers who become family? The wild landscapes that change our perspective? The freedom of discovering that we’re capable of far more than we ever imagined?

I wanted to create a guide that didn’t just tell women what to pack, but helped them feel capable of packing up and going in the first place.
One that combined the practical knowledge I spent four years figuring out with the encouragement I needed when I was that clueless woman standing in a bike shop in Vietnam.

And to answer a question I’ve already received: Is this guide only for women?

Not at all!

While I’ve dedicated several sections to female-specific gear, safety, and experiences, the vast majority of the guide is useful for anyone interested in traveling far by bicycle. It’s also a great gift for a woman in your life who’s been dreaming about her own two-wheeled adventure.

The Women’s Bikepacking Guide is Available Now

Get the guide here: womensbikepackingguide.com

Every purchase supports my work as an independent filmmaker, writer, and cyclist, and means more to me than you know.
I’d genuinely love to hear from you. Where are you dreaming of riding? What questions do you have? And if you’ve picked up the guide, what resonated with you most?

Because one of the greatest things four years on the road taught me is that even when we ride alone, we’re never really doing it alone.
I wrote this guide for every woman with a wild, quiet dream tucked away in a drawer labeled someday. Open the drawer. The road belongs to you, too.
Here’s to more women out there, more adventures by bicycle, and the courage to turn someday into now.

Happy tailwinds!

– McKenzie
